message.content:
Here are a few popular sushi spots in Tokyo that you might want to try:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sushi Saito** | Ginza | Michelin‑starred, intimate setting, seasonal Omakase |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | 3 Michelin stars, meticulous preparation, small tasting menu |
| **Sushi Jiro (Jiro Sushi)** | Roppongi | Famous from *Jiro Dreams of Sushi*, 3 Michelin stars, limited seating |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Known for fresh fish and long lines, great value |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | 24/7 service, casual atmosphere, good for quick bites |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic sushi experience, high quality ingredients |
| **Sushi Sugita** | Shinjuku | 2 Michelin stars, innovative techniques |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ebisu | 2 Michelin stars, focus on seasonal ingredients |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Shibuya | 1 Michelin star, modern presentation |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Marunouchi | 1 Michelin star, elegant setting |

These places range from high‑end Michelin‑starred experiences to more casual, yet still excellent, options. If you’re planning a visit, it’s wise to make reservations well in advance—especially for the Michelin‑starred spots. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
